findings.title: All playground CTAs on landing page point to a path that does not exist
findings.description: index.html header nav (line 34), hero CTA (line 54) and all six 'Try this in playground' links (93,130,168,217,276,323) target ./playground/index.html; app.js:47,50 rewrites try-links to the same ./playground/ prefix. No website/playground/ directory exists (website/ has 10 files, no subdir), and website/README.md says deployment is 'copying the website/ directory'. benchmarks.html:196 uses ../playground/index.html instead - the two pages contradict each other and index.html is broken under both layouts.
findings.root_cause: Relative playground path chosen for an in-website copy of the playground that was never created; benchmarks.html later used the correct sibling-relative path without fixing index.html.
findings.impact: The landing page's primary conversion action ('Try in playground', 7 links total) 404s for every visitor under the repo's own deployment instructions; 'Try this' demo links never open with pre-loaded code.
findings.recommendation: Change index.html nav/hero and app.js to ../playground/index.html (matching benchmarks.html) and update website/README.md to document that website/ and playground/ must be deployed as sibling directories.
findings.fix_guide: 1) In website/index.html replace all 8 occurrences of ./playground/ with ../playground/. 2) In website/app.js lines 47 and 50 do the same. 3) In website/README.md Deploy section, state that playground/ must be copied as a sibling of website/ (or served from repo root). 4) Add a Playwright assertion that the resolved href returns HTTP 200 against the repo-root static server.

effort_estimate.breakdown: href replacements 5m; app.js 2m; README deploy note 3m; optional Playwright 200-check 5m

detection_method.query: href="./playground/index.html" in website/*; glob website/**/* shows no playground subdir

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path website\index.html,website\app.js -Pattern '\./playground/index\.html' | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count; Test-Path website\playground; Select-String -Path website\benchmarks.html -Pattern '\.\./playground/index\.html'

confidence.rationale: Directory absence verified by glob of website/**; internal contradiction between index.html and benchmarks.html paths confirms one is wrong; README deploy model makes ./playground unresolvable.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Only failure mode would be an intended deployment that copies playground/ inside website/, which no doc describes; benchmarks.html using ../ proves the sibling layout is canonical.

findings.title: Book claims plain .map 'already fans out across cores' via Rayon with a runs-today marker; codegen emits no Rayon
findings.description: Section 4.2 (marked runs end-to-end) states the .map example 'already fans out across cores', that on 8 cores 'the eight multiplications literally run on eight cores simultaneously', and 'The compiler inserted all of it' (Rayon). Grep of crates/buff-lang-codegen-rust/src finds zero par_iter/into_par_iter/rayon emission; rayon exists only in buff-lang-runtime/src/cpu.rs CpuDispatcher, used for runtime dispatch fallback, not for ordinary .map lowering.
findings.root_cause: Heterogeneous-compute pitch (README:44 'emits both a Rayon path and a WGSL shader') was carried into the book as a present-tense runs-today claim without verifying what codegen actually emits for un-annotated .map calls.
findings.impact: Users choosing Buff over Go/Rust for free automatic data parallelism get sequential iterator code today; a factually false performance claim marked as verified-runnable in the official guide.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite 4.2 to say .map lowers to a sequential iterator today and CPU-parallel (Rayon) execution happens only through the runtime dispatcher (e.g. @prefer(gpu) fallback), or downgrade the section marker from runs-today to partial.

fix_examples.before: This already fans out across cores. On an 8-core machine the eight multiplications literally run on eight cores simultaneously.
fix_examples.after: Today this lowers to a sequential iterator. CPU-parallel (Rayon) execution engages via the runtime dispatcher - e.g. when an @prefer(gpu) function falls back to CPU with a large input - not for plain .map calls (see 4.3).

findings.fix_guide: 1) Edit book/src/chapter-4.md lines 56-76 to describe sequential lowering with a pointer to dispatcher-based parallelism. 2) Cross-check README.md:42-46 wording for the same overstatement. 3) Add a codegen snapshot test asserting whether .map emits par_iter, so docs and codegen cannot drift silently.

effort_estimate.breakdown: rewrite 10m; README cross-check 5m; optional snapshot test 15m

detection_method.query: par_iter|into_par_iter|rayon in crates/buff-lang-codegen-rust/src (0 hits) vs book chapter-4 'fans out across cores'

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path book\src\chapter-4.md -Pattern 'fans out across cores'; Get-ChildItem -Recurse crates\buff-lang-codegen-rust\src -Include *.rs | Select-String -Pattern 'par_iter|into_par_iter' | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

confidence.rationale: Zero parallel-iterator emission in codegen src is verified; small residual risk that parallelism enters via a crate the generated code links that was not grepped (e.g. prelude_types runtime references) - hence not 0.95.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Claim text and codegen absence both read directly; only uncertainty is an indirect Rayon path outside codegen src, which would still contradict 'plain .map fans out'.

findings.title: Benchmarks summary card says 7 fixtures; tables, JSON and harness define 6
findings.description: The 'Fixtures' summary card shows 7, but the Compile Time / Codegen Hash / Binary Size / Dispatch tables list 6 fixtures, the raw JSON block contains exactly 6 entries, and the producing harness (buff bench, cli.rs:1192-1194) documents 'the 6 canonical names'. The page is the project's public performance-evidence surface.
findings.root_cause: Card value hand-edited or copied from a different capture run than the embedded JSON/table without reconciliation.
findings.impact: Data-integrity defect on the marketing benchmarks page: a competitor or evaluator recounting fixtures finds the headline number contradicted by the page's own data two scroll-lengths below.
findings.recommendation: Change the summary card to 6, and ideally generate all summary cards from the same embedded JSON so the page cannot self-contradict on future captures.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Set card value to 6 (or derive counts from the JSON via a tiny script at capture time). 2) Regenerate the page from capture_t22_baseline output so card/table/JSON always agree. 3) Keep the honest capture-date/commit footer as is.

detection_method.query: summary-card-value '7' vs <tr> fixture rows and JSON 'fixtures' keys on same page

confidence.rationale: Directly counted on one page plus harness doc; no interpretation needed.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Pure arithmetic mismatch inside a single file; '7' cannot be justified by any grouping of the 6 listed rows.

findings.title: Error Code Handbook omits 6 of the 62 stable codes; range headers contradict enum and docs/errors site
findings.description: Section headers claim 'Parsing - E1101-E1109' (line 131) and 'Type-checking - E1201-E1209' (line 184), but code.rs defines E1110 (comptime malformed, line 119) and E1210-E1214 (comptime eval/IO/reflection, dyn-trait object, lifetime, lines 152-167), and docs/errors/ ships exactly 62 E1xxx pages matching the enum's 62 variants. The handbook documents 56/62, so its stated ranges are factually stale against the two sources it cites as canonical.
findings.root_cause: E1110 and E1210-E1214 were appended (v1.13+ comptime and v1.34 dyn-trait work) without updating chapter-8's section ranges or adding entries.
findings.impact: Users searching the handbook for comptime (E1110/E1210-E1212) or dyn-trait (E1213/E1214) codes find nothing, undermining the 'every code is documented' stability story the chapter leads with.
findings.recommendation: Add sections for E1110 and E1210-E1214 (copy explanation/fix from code.rs docs + docs/errors pages) and correct the two range headers to E1101-E1110 and E1201-E1214.

fix_examples.after:

## 8.4 Type-checking â€” `E1201`â€“`E1214`

findings.fix_guide: 1) Insert E1110 subsection from code.rs:119 doc + docs/errors/E1110.html. 2) Insert five subsections for E1210-E1214 from code.rs:152-167 + matching HTML pages. 3) Fix both range headers. 4) Consider a test that diffs chapter-8 code mentions against ErrorCode variants.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 6 subsections x 8m + header edits 5m + link check 7m

detection_method.query: chapter-8 range headers vs '^    [A-Z]\w+,$' count (62) in code.rs and docs/errors glob (62 pages)

findings.verification_command: (Select-String -Path crates\buff-lang-error\src\code.rs -Pattern '^    [A-Z]\w+,$').Count; (Get-ChildItem docs\errors\E*.html).Count; Select-String -Path book\src\chapter-8.md -Pattern 'E1101â€“E1109|E1201â€“E1209'; Select-String -Path book\src\chapter-8.md -Pattern 'E1110|E1210' | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

confidence.rationale: 62 enum variants, 62 HTML pages, and chapter-8's absent E1110/E1210-E1214 mentions all directly verified by count grep.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Chapter-8 itself declares the enum + site canonical; the mismatch is mechanical, and chapter-8's 'when in doubt, the site wins' caveat does not make its range headers true.

findings.title: '~95% of user code never knows async exists' is an unverifiable quantitative claim repeated across 6 surfaces
findings.description: README.md:52, book chapter-6.md:458, chapter-9.md:202, and docs-site/content (onboarding/rust-developers.md:26, language/async.md:23, cookbook/async.md:11) all state ~95% (or 'About 95%'/'Around 95%') of user code never encounters async. No benchmark, corpus analysis, or measurement in the repo substantiates the figure; buff-lang-types/src/async_analysis.rs implements propagation analysis but emits no such statistic.
findings.root_cause: A rhetorical estimate hardened into a repeated pseudo-precise statistic and copy-pasted across README, book, and docs-site.
findings.impact: A precise-sounding number with no methodology is exactly the kind of claim competitors and HN-style reviewers discredit; it also risks contradicting future measured data.
findings.recommendation: Soften to a qualitative claim ('most user code never needs await; async propagates automatically') or link to a reproducible measurement; keep one canonical wording and reference it from the other five surfaces.

fix_examples.before: ~95% of user code never knows async exists.
fix_examples.after: Most user code never knows async exists â€” no `await`, no colored functions; async propagates up the call graph automatically.

findings.fix_guide: 1) Pick the qualitative wording in README.md:52. 2) Apply the same wording in book/src/chapter-6.md:458, chapter-9.md:202, docs-site/content/onboarding/rust-developers.md:26, docs-site/content/language/async.md:23, docs-site/content/cookbook/async.md:11. 3) If a number is desired, add a scripts/ analysis over examples/ and cite it.

detection_method.query: 95% across *.md,*.html (6 hits, no measurement backing in-repo)

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path README.md,book\src\chapter-6.md,book\src\chapter-9.md,docs-site\content\onboarding\rust-developers.md,docs-site\content\language\async.md,docs-site\content\cookbook\async.md -Pattern '95%'; Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Include *.md,*.rs | Select-String -Pattern '95\s*(percent|%)' | Where-Object {$_.Filename -notmatch 'README|chapter|async|rust-developers|cookbook'} | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count

confidence.rationale: Absence of any backing measurement verified by repo-wide grep for the figure; residual chance a plan doc derives it heuristically, which would still not be a measurement.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Flagging only the unverifiable precision, not the qualitative async story, which is real (async_analysis.rs exists); aspirational-vs-factual framing is clearly separated in the recommendation.

findings.title: GPU dispatch marketed in present tense while the book admits it is not wired end-to-end
findings.description: README:42-46 says the compiler 'emits both a Rayon path and a WGSL shader, then the runtime picks at execution time' and :56-59 promises binaries that 'dispatch hot loops to the GPU'; website/index.html:48-51 echoes it. But book chapter-4.md:115-119 (marked partial) states 'End-to-end GPU dispatch from buff run requires the wgpu runtime linkage wired through the CLI's single-file pipeline', and the project's own benchmarks page records '0 GPU dispatches'. WGSL codegen + runtime are real and unit-tested, but the shipped buff run path does not execute GPU shaders.
findings.root_cause: v1.0 positioning copy predates the honest partial-capability markers added in the book; the README/website were not synced when the end-to-end wiring was found unfinished.
findings.impact: Positioning incoherence for a dev tool competing on capability: a user trying the headline GPU feature gets CPU fallback silently; the discrepancy between README/website and the book/benchmarks is discoverable within minutes.
findings.recommendation: Add a status qualifier to README idea 3 and the website hero ('GPU dispatch: shader codegen + runtime shipped; end-to-end buff run wiring in progress'), and link chapter-4's partial marker so all four surfaces tell one story.

fix_examples.before: Invisible heterogeneous computing. The same Buff function can run on CPU or be dispatched to GPU automatically â€” the compiler analyzes arithmetic intensity and emits both a Rayon path and a WGSL shader, then the runtime picks at execution time.
fix_examples.after: Invisible heterogeneous computing (in progress). The compiler emits a WGSL shader next to your function and the runtime routes CPU/GPU; shader codegen + runtime are shipped and tested â€” end-to-end GPU execution through `buff run` is the last wiring step (see Book ch. 4).

findings.fix_guide: 1) Qualify README.md:42-46 and :56-59. 2) Add one line to website/index.html hero body near line 48-51. 3) Verify chapter-4:115-119 stays the canonical status note and link it. 4) Re-run website Playwright tests (copy-only change).

effort_estimate.breakdown: README edits 10m; website edit 5m; cross-link + review 10m

detection_method.query: README present-tense GPU claims vs chapter-4 partial marker and benchmarks.html '0 GPU dispatches'

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path README.md -Pattern 'dispatched to GPU automatically|dispatches hot loops'; Select-String -Path book\src\chapter-4.md -Pattern 'End-to-end GPU dispatch'; Select-String -Path website\benchmarks.html -Pattern 'GPU dispatches' -Context 1,1

confidence.rationale: The book's own partial marker plus 0-dispatch benchmark evidence make the overstatement unambiguous; uncertainty only on whether an unreleased local build wires GPU end-to-end.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Not claiming the feature is fake - WGSL/runtime crates and tests exist; flagging only present-tense marketing of a not-yet-wired path, which the repo's own ch4 marker confirms.
